w10_T4_004235: In the morning the Ashford grain mill loaded each cart with 4 sacks of 44 kilograms and then tipped in 78 kilograms of loose grain, and it sent out 7 carts like that every hour. In the afternoon the foreman confirmed the mill had run at that rate for 7 hours that day. In the evening he noted that the mill had done exactly the same on each of 6 days that week, and then took in a 20-kilogram sack returned by a customer. How many kilograms of grain did the mill handle that week, counting the returned sack?
w10_T4_004236: In the morning 47 children arrived at the summer camp, then 53 more came on the second bus and 80 on the third. In the afternoon the organisers counted that 4 camps of exactly that size were meeting at the park. In the evening all of those children were split equally into 6 teams for the campfire games. How many children are on each team?
w10_T4_004251: A relief group had 153 blankets in each of its warehouses, and a donor tripled the number in every warehouse. Then 136 blankets were handed out from each warehouse during the cold snap. The group has 7 warehouses, all stocked and used identically. A school then collected 36 blankets and a church collected 65, and both lots were added to the group's total. How many blankets does the relief group have now?
w10_T4_004254: In the morning each of the theatre's 2 box-office windows had 180 tickets and sold 64 of them, so the manager combined what the 2 windows had left into one drawer. The show runs for 3 hours. In the afternoon 104 tickets were sold from the drawer, and 108 more went to a school group. In the evening 2 tickets were found torn and thrown away. How many tickets are in the drawer now?
w10_T4_004259: Each of Wes's 4 photo albums has 176 slots, but 96 slots in every album are empty, and the rest hold one photo each. His cousin Lia gave him 48 loose photos, a smaller number than Wes already had. Wes then printed a second copy of every photo he had, so he had 2 of each. He later bought 68 postcards to keep with the photos. How many photos and postcards does Wes have now?
w10_T4_004268: Candle maker Femi weighs wax in grams, though the supplier sells it by the kilogram and he knows a thousand grams make a kilogram. This morning he poured 9 candles in each batch with 163 grams of wax per candle, and he made 5 batches. He then sold 4574 grams of that wax, still unset, to a craft shop next door. A trainee returned 34 grams of wax trimmings to the bench. How many grams of wax does Femi have left?
w10_T4_004271: A syrup maker keeps track of its stock in millilitres, converting to litres only for the shipping forms, since a thousand millilitres make a litre. Each bottle is filled with 235 millilitres and then 22 millilitres is drawn off as a quality sample. The bottles are packed 8 to a crate and 7 crates to a pallet, and 3 pallets make up the whole stock. A cooling failure then spoiled 9923 millilitres of the stock, which was poured away. How many millilitres of syrup are in the stock now?
w10_T4_004272: Ray gathered 213 conkers from under the horse chestnut tree, and 5 of them split when they fell. His friend Sol brought 52 conkers of his own, far fewer than Ray had, and tipped them into Ray's bag. The 4 friends in their gang then shared the bag equally, which took half an hour of counting. Sol found 4 more conkers on the walk home and kept them. How many conkers does Sol have now?
w10_T4_004274: In the morning each of the pizzeria's 4 trays held 157 dough balls, and 107 balls from every tray were used up for the lunch orders. In the afternoon 49 dough balls were sold uncooked to a customer. In the evening every dough ball left was baked into a pizza and cut into 8 slices, and 80 of those slices were given to the staff for their dinner. How many slices are left for the evening customers?
w10_T4_004276: In the morning each of the 5 crates at the harbour restaurant held 162 oysters, and 90 oysters from each crate were shucked for the brunch service. In the afternoon a fisherman dropped off 37 more oysters. In the evening 245 oysters were served at dinner, and a late delivery brought 48 more. How many oysters does the restaurant have now?
w10_T4_004279: In the morning the road trip was planned to take 100 minutes, but a shortcut cut 20 minutes off, and the driving was divided equally among the 4 friends in the car, which has 5 seats. In the afternoon Ines drove her share plus 10 extra minutes because of roadworks. In the evening she drove exactly the same amount again on the way back, so her total driving for the day was 2 times her afternoon amount. She logs her driving in minutes, though the insurance form asks for hours and she knows sixty minutes make an hour. How many minutes did Ines drive that day?
w10_T4_004285: In the morning Nico packed 58 grapes in his lunch box, and his friend Ada, who had only 54 grapes and so slightly fewer than Nico, tipped hers into his box so he could carry them. At morning break Nico ate 41 grapes from the box. In the afternoon he gave 43 grapes to the football team. In the evening he ate 17 more on the bus home. How many grapes are left in Nico's lunch box?
w10_T4_004287: The Riverbend chess club had 61 members in January, and 20 of them let their memberships lapse. During the spring drive Rin recruited 71 new members while Kai recruited 75, so Kai brought in more than Rin, and all of those recruits joined. The annual fee is 15 dollars. A merger with the library club then added 69 members. How many members does the chess club have now?
w10_T4_004289: In the morning Farmer Ines had 18 cartons of eggs on the shelf; 1 carton was crushed and thrown out, and a customer bought a dozen cartons. Each carton left held 6 eggs, so Ines emptied them and counted the loose eggs. In the afternoon a second collection from the hens gave her exactly as many loose eggs again, making her loose-egg count 2 times what it had been. In the evening she packed all the loose eggs equally into 6 boxes for the market, noting that the wholesaler invoices by the dozen even though she counts in single eggs. How many eggs are in each box?
w10_T4_004295: Kai had 111 cents in his pocket-money jar and counts in cents, though his allowance is set in dollars and he knows a hundred cents make a dollar. He lost 1 cent through a hole in his pocket, spent 36 cents on a pencil, 61 cents on a comic and 7 cents on a sweet, all from the jar. His mother then made whatever was left in the jar 2 times as large. His uncle later dropped 58 cents into the jar. How many cents are in Kai's jar now?
w10_T4_004297: A vineyard block was planted with 215 vines, then 39 more were added, and 73 vines died in a frost. The grower then tripled the number of vines in the block by planting the empty land around it. A disease forced the removal of 267 vines. Each remaining vine yields 8 kilograms of grapes at harvest. How many kilograms of grapes will the block yield?
w10_T4_004299: The school science storeroom received 2 crates of test tubes with 121 tubes in each, and those were all the tubes it had. During the first week 157 tubes were taken out for experiments, and 72 more went to the chemistry club. A supplier then delivered 40 tubes to the storeroom. Then 44 tubes were found cracked and thrown out. How many test tubes are in the storeroom now?
w10_T4_004304: In the morning each of the 7 milk tanks at the Fenwick dairy held 218 litres, and 151 litres were drawn from every tank for the morning bottling. The dairy has 30 cows. In the afternoon 14 litres were added from a late milking, and then 408 litres were sold to the cheese maker. In the evening the neighbouring dairy reported exactly the same amount of milk left as Fenwick, so the co-op combined the 2 amounts for the night collection. How many litres of milk did the co-op collect that night?
w10_T4_004309: Jun had 40 trading cards and gave 39 of them to his sister Lin, who had none, so Lin then held far more cards than Jun. The tournament that weekend had 16 players. Jun won 42 cards during the tournament, then gave 18 to a friend and lost 20 in the final round. A dealer at the venue offered 9 cards for every card Jun still had, and Jun swapped all of his. A second dealer then offered 2 cards for each of those, and Jun swapped again. How many cards does Jun have now?
w10_T4_004310: Dana and Eli were fencing a paddock. Each roll of wire they opened held 152 metres; from every roll Dana used 68 metres and Eli used 28 metres, so Dana used more wire than Eli. They opened 3 rolls, used them all the same way, and kept the leftover wire from each roll in one pile. Their neighbour then handed over exactly as much wire as was in the pile, so the pile became 2 times as long. How many metres of wire are in the pile now?
w10_T4_004311: In the morning the quarry had 221 tonnes of gravel on the pad, and 17 more tonnes were crushed before noon, then 5 tonnes were swept back from the edges. In the afternoon the gravel on the pad was divided equally among 3 trucks for the first run. In the evening the site manager worked out that the road job would need 7 loads of exactly the size each truck had carried. How many tonnes of gravel does the road job need?
w10_T4_004313: The island ferry has 193 seats. On each crossing this week 106 seats were taken by commuters, 47 by tourists and 8 by crew members, and the rest stayed empty. The ferry makes the crossing twice a day. Over 5 days at that rate, how many empty seats were there in total?
w10_T4_004314: In the morning the rental shack had 24 kayaks lined up on the beach, and 32 more were unloaded from the truck. In the afternoon 53 kayaks came back from a group tour and 22 came back from private renters. In the evening 95 kayaks were loaded onto trailers for winter storage. How many kayaks are left on the beach?
w10_T4_004317: The sports club measures juice in millilitres, though the supplier sells it by the litre and everyone knows a thousand millilitres make a litre. In the morning the volunteers poured 191 millilitres into each of the 6 cups on a tray and filled 9 trays, then emptied all of it equally into 6 coolers. In the afternoon the players drank 1684 millilitres from the red cooler. In the evening the coach topped up the red cooler so that it held 3 times what had been left in it. How many millilitres of juice are in the red cooler now?
w10_T4_004319: Mo had 66 cents left after the school fair, and he counts in cents though his teacher writes prices in dollars and he knows a hundred cents make a dollar. He spent 29 cents on a lolly, while his friend Ria spent 36 cents of his money on a ribbon for him, so Ria spent more of it than Mo did. Each of the 4 friends in his group had exactly the same amount left as Mo, and they pooled it all. They spent 3 cents of the pool on a gumball, then a change machine gave them 8 cents for every cent in the pool, which had been sitting there for a dozen minutes. The pool was finally shared equally among the 4 friends. How many cents did each friend get?
